title: Cynosure omni-query throughput & cost scan (POC workshop notes)
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures the benchmark sweep we ran for Cynosure (omni-query product) during the Oct 2028 onsite POC workshop. Goal was to characterize latency/throughput tradeoffs and produce a pragmatic cost model for the three deployment options they care about: Hosted API (redwood-hosted), Dedicated GPU pool, and Private (VPC-onprem patch). We focused on: short chat style queries (8–40 tokens), search/rerank-style prompts (40–150 tokens), and long-document summarization (600–1500 tokens).

High-level takeaways (short):
- Under mixed real-world traffic (80% short chat, 15% rerank, 5% long summary), a single Dedicated A100-80GB instance (4-card node, queueless serving) with batching tuned to 8ms target latency sustained ~1.9k QPS aggregate for short requests (p95 ~ 36ms) and overall platform cost estimate of $0.009/token-equivalent (see model).
- Hosted API with autoscale and prefix cache reduced observed p95 for rerank by ~22% compared to naive Dedicated config because of warm KV cache and model variant routing; but hosted cost profile ended up ~15–25% higher per-effective-query due to premium routing and burst capacity premiums for their expected burst windows.
- Private VPC onprem with H100 instances excelled for long summaries (throughput up to 60 reqs/min for 1500-token jobs) but suffered from cold-start tail for singleton elastic workers; recommendation: keep hot-pool and enable pre-warming for scheduled batch summary jobs.

Test matrix and environment:
- Dates: runs 2028-10-03 to 2028-10-10 (this doc records aggregated notes).
- Hardware tested: H100 (80GB) single-card + 4x pod cluster, A100 (80GB) single-card and 4-card node, CPU inference nodes for orchestration only (m6i-large).
- Model variants: Omni-7B (int8-quant), Omni-13B (fp16), Omni-33B (fp16, no quant), and an ensemble fallback path that routes long summaries to Omni-33B.
- Server runtime: Redwood serving runtime v2.9.1 with continuous batching enabled, auto-prefix cache enabled, and KV-cache TTL=12h for rerank prefix keys.
- Load generator: custom script (github link above) driving mixed-profile traffic with Poisson arrivals and configurable microburst windows.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency (server-to-client), tokens/sec, effective QPS (requests/sec weighted by token length), GPU utilization, and estimated cost per 1k effective-queries (cost model described below).

Workload profiles:
- Short-chat: 8–40 tokens output; typical prompt 20 tokens; latency SLO target: p95 < 50ms.
- Rerank-search: 40–150 tokens output; many repeated prefix tokens (benefit from prefix/KV cache); SLO target: p95 < 120ms.
- Long-summary: 600–1500 tokens output; throughput-oriented, SLO target: p95 < 8s (not tight but cost-sensitive).
- Traffic mix used for mixed-run: 80/15/5 short/rerank/long. Microburst windows: 30s windows at 3x baseline QPS every 10 minutes to emulate promotional pulses.

Key experimental permutations:
- Batching window: 0ms (no batching), 4ms, 8ms, 16ms target latency caps; continuous batching buffer size varied 8–256 tokens per batch.
- KV cache: on vs off; hot-cache hit rates measured per-run.
- Model routing policy: single model vs fallback (small model primary, fallback to 33B if quality threshold not met).
- Cold-start: scaling from 0 to target QPS with 0s pre-warm vs 30s warm pool.

Representative results (mixed-profile, Dedicated A100 4-card node, batching 8ms):
- Short-chat (Omni-7B int8): p50 12ms, p95 36ms, p99 90ms; sustained short QPS ~1900; GPU util ~62%.
- Rerank (Omni-13B fp16 with KV): p50 28ms, p95 98ms, p99 220ms; cache hit ratio 67% -> reduced compute tokens by ~48% vs cold path.
- Long-summary (Omni-33B fp16): p50 2.9s, p95 5.4s, p99 8.6s; throughput 55 req/min per node.
- Aggregate effective QPS (mixed): ~530 req/s weighted; average latency composite p95 ~310ms (long jobs dominate tail).

Cost model (simplified, rough numbers for customer budgeting):
- Assumptions: A100-4 node monthly amortized cost $14,000 (cloud equivalent), H100-4 node $20,000, hosted premium margin +25% on base infra, tokens billed equivalent based on normalized effective-token metric.
- Dedicated (amortized + runtime infra): estimated $0.007–0.012 per effective-query depending on batching and cache efficiency.
- Hosted API estimate: $0.009–0.015 per effective-query (higher on microburst days due to reserved burst capacity).
- Private onprem: capital + ops; per-query operating cost dominated by infra amortization and SRE; wide band $0.005–0.01 depending on utilization and headcount amortization.

Observations and actionable recommendations:
1) Batching sweet spot: for Cynosure's mix, 8ms batching cap produced the best throughput/latency balance. 4ms reduced throughput by ~11% but improved p95 by ~6ms. 16ms saved cost modestly but hurt p95 for short-chat beyond SLO.
2) KV-prefix cache is critical for rerank: enabling cache cut rerank compute by ~48% and p95 by ~22%. Recommendation: persist top-500 query prefixes and maintain LRU eviction tuned to 100k unique keys.
3) Model selection: run short-chat on Omni-7B quantized; move complex long summaries to Omni-33B. For mid-tail rerank, Omni-13B fp16 gave best p95/perf. Consider a staged fallback (7B -> 13B -> 33B) with quality checks at 75% confidence thresholds.
4) Cold-start mitigation: for Private deployments expect larger cold-start p99 tails for scheduled batch jobs. Keep a small hot pool sized to average burst size during business hours; for expected night-window batch runs, schedule pre-warm jobs 2 minutes before run.
5) Autoscaling knobs: prefer proactive scale-up for 30s microbursts rather than reactive; reactive autoscale adds 1–4s cold-start tail depending on node spin-up.
6) Cost vs latency knobs: customers can trade lower cost via higher batching and more aggressive quantization; present two price/latency profiles to product managers (latency-first vs cost-first).

Open questions and risks noted during workshop:
- Quality regressions with int8 quant for some rare instruction-following prompts; need dedicated eval suite for Cynosure prompt set before moving 7B quant to production.
- PCIe/NIC contention seen on one H100 node during simultaneous long-summary runs; unclear whether cloud placement or scheduling caused the degradation. Further isolating tests needed.
- Cold-region routing increases p95 for short-chat by ~30–45ms; if Cynosure wants global low-latency experience, they should provision regional Dedicated capacity or use hosted with region-affinity routing.

Next steps / action items (owner + ETA):
- Create Cynosure-specific eval harness: Mateo (owner) — ETA 2028-10-18.
- Run deeper H100 contention test with dedicated NIC profiling: Priya (owner) — ETA 2028-10-21.
- Draft customer-facing cost/latency options one-pager: Ava (owner) + Marketing review — ETA 2028-10-14.
- Implement KV cache policy prototype with LRU counter and metrics export to console: Eng-runtime (RFC) — ETA 2028-11-01.

Appendix (notes, raw observations):
- During the 10/05 microburst run we saw a transient p99 spike (short-chat) to 640ms when batcher aggregated 128 short messages due to a bug in request size estimation — fixed by filter to cap short-chat batches to 32.
- Observed tokenization variance across clients; recommend standardizing on UTF-8 normalizer and the shared tokenizer bundle (repo link in artifacts).
- Sample trace excerpts (simplified): 1) Short-chat path: request -> routing -> KV miss -> batch assemble (18ms) -> compute 12ms -> stream start 6ms -> client ack; 2) Rerank hot: request -> KV hit -> bypass decode step -> compute 18ms -> stream.

Meeting notes (raw):
- Cynosure PM prioritized 95th percentile latency for chat as top metric (strict), but allowed 500–800ms for long-summaries if cost improved.
- Security team asked about KMS integration for Private deployments; we confirmed Redwood supports KMS/HSM envelope keys and will run a separate security checklist.

If anything here needs re-running or deeper granularity (per-model kernel timings, per-layer memory pressure), call out which axis and we'll add to the next sweep scope.

-- Ava
